passage: The mid-semester marks went up on the notice board of their Bengaluru college, and a small crowd formed. Megha, top of the class for three semesters, had scraped a 61 in Signals. Francis nudged Samir, trying not to grin. "Miss Perfect finally slipped." He said it low, but his eyes were shining. Samir looked at the board, then at Francis. He didn't laugh. Later, walking to the canteen, he asked, "Why does her 61 make you so happy?" Francis shrugged. "She makes it look easy. I study till two and still get 70." "So it's more about you than her?" Francis kicked a stone. "Maybe. Yeah." They bought tea. Francis didn't mention Megha again.

qa.q: What mark did Megha get in Signals?
What was Francis feeling under the grin?
qa.a: Envy and frustration: he studies till two and still gets 70, so Megha's slip felt satisfying because she makes it look easy.

qa.q: What did Samir choose instead of laughing, and why did it help?
qa.a: He stayed quiet at the board and later gently asked why the 61 made Francis so happy, which helped Francis see it was about his own struggle.

qa.q: How might Megha feel if she had heard "Miss Perfect finally slipped"?
qa.a: She would likely feel hurt and isolated, already dealing with a low mark and now being enjoyed by classmates.

grounding: A student sees Francis enjoy a top student's low mark and, instead of joining in, gently asks what the envy is about.

passage: "Did you see? Dev's project got rejected by the department. Mister Gold Medal." Kamal was grinning over his phone in the library corridor. Arohi kept her voice low. "You look really pleased." "I'm not pleased. It's just funny. He always acts like he's above everyone." "Did he act like that with you?" "Not exactly. He just... gets everything." "Mm." Arohi waited. "If you could have one of his things, what would it be?" Kamal was quiet. "The professor asking my opinion. The way he asks Dev." "That's a real thing to want." "Yeah." Kamal put the phone away. "Don't tell anyone I was gloating." "You weren't, really. You were jealous. Different." "Wow, thanks." But he was almost smiling.

qa.a: "If you could have one of his things, what would it be?" It moved Kamal from mocking Dev to naming his own wish, without shaming him.

qa.a: The gloating could have spread, leaving Dev to face mockery on top of the rejection.

subtype: Friend notices glee at another's downfall [Observer]
passage: I'm Bhavna. Last month at our coaching centre, the topper, Farzana, froze during a mock interview in front of everyone and walked out. Afterwards, in the stairwell, my friend Kunal did an impression of her freezing. Two boys laughed. I could see Kunal's face: bright, almost hungry, enjoying it more than the joke deserved. I didn't laugh. I didn't lecture him either. I just stayed quiet and went down the stairs. Kunal caught up with me. "What, too mean?" "Kind of," I said. "Is it about Farzana, or about the interviews?" He went quiet. Then he admitted he'd been turned down by two colleges and she had got into both. Looking back, I'm glad I didn't join in. It was easier than I thought, just not laughing.

qa.q: What did Kunal do in the stairwell?
qa.a: An impression of Farzana freezing.

qa.q: What did Bhavna notice in Kunal's face, and what did it suggest?
qa.a: It was bright, almost hungry, suggesting Kunal was enjoying Farzana's slip more than the joke deserved, most likely out of envy.

qa.q: What choice did Bhavna make in the stairwell, and why did it work?
qa.a: Bhavna didn't laugh or lecture, and then gently asked whether it was about Farzana or the interviews, which let Kunal admit his rejections.

qa.q: How might Farzana feel if she learned about the stairwell impression?
qa.a: Hurt and embarrassed twice over, first by freezing and then by being mocked by classmates.

grounding: A student sees a friend enjoy a topper's slip, stays quiet instead of laughing, and gently asks what lies behind it.

Tutor's note, Year 2 seminar group, Friday. Mrs Anita Kurian.
During today's presentations, Harshal, usually the strongest in the group, lost his place, dropped his notes and had to start over. Yamini, two seats from me, put her hand over her mouth. Her shoulders were shaking. She was laughing, silently, and trying to hide it.
Her friend Ramesh, beside her, did not join in. He didn't scold her either. After the session I passed them in the corridor and heard him ask quietly, "What is it about Harshal that gets to you?" Yamini was silent, then said, "He makes it look easy. I work twice as hard for half the marks."
I will not mention the laughter to Yamini. I'll offer her a meeting about her marks, and I'll make sure to thank Harshal for starting over.

qa.q: What happened to Harshal during his presentation?
qa.a: He lost his place, dropped his notes and had to start over.

qa.q: What does Yamini's answer to Ramesh reveal about her laughter?
qa.a: It suggests envy: Harshal seems to succeed easily while she works twice as hard for half the marks.

qa.q: Which choice by Ramesh worked, and why?
qa.a: He neither joined in nor scolded, and instead asked what bothered her, which let Yamini name the envy herself.

qa.q: How might Harshal have felt if he had seen Yamini laughing?
qa.a: He might have felt humiliated and hurt, since he was already struggling in front of the group.

grounding: A tutor records a friend who sees a classmate secretly enjoy the top student's slip and gently asks about the envy.

passage:
Thursday

Weird afternoon. In the physics lab, Latika, the topper, mixed up two readings in front of Professor Das and got told, "I expected better from you." Ayesha, next to me, kicked my ankle under the bench and mouthed, "Finally." She was grinning into her lab manual the whole next hour. She even started typing to our group, then deleted it.
I didn't grin back. I didn't lecture her either. On the walk to the bus, I just asked, "Why does Latika bother you so much?" She walked for a bit and said, "Because Papa asks every single week why I'm not like her." Oh.
We didn't fix anything. We bought corn from the cart and talked about her papa. I think the grin was never really about Latika.
Kavitha

qa.q: What did Professor Das say to Latika?
qa.a: "I expected better from you."

qa.q: What does Ayesha's grin and deleted message suggest she was feeling?
qa.a: She seemed secretly pleased by Latika's slip, but part of her also knew it wasn't right to share it.

qa.q: What went well in how Kavitha handled Ayesha's glee?
qa.a: Kavitha didn't join in or lecture, and gently asked why Latika bothered her, which uncovered the pressure from her papa.

qa.q: How might Latika have felt being told off in front of Professor Das?
qa.a: Latika probably felt embarrassed and pressured, carrying a reputation that makes even small slips sting.
